title: Japanese Town Struggles with Violent Monkeys
paragraphs: Yugawara, a hot spring town in Kanagawa Prefecture in Japan, is having serious problems with a group of wild monkeys.
The monkeys are Japanese macaques. Monkeys have lived in the area around Yugawara since 1955. But one group, or troop, called "T1" has become a big problem. The troop has about 20 monkeys.

According to reports, the T1 troop was believed to be responsible for 6,054 incidents in 2025. These included attacking people, stealing, damaging property and bothering people. In September 2026, a man in his 40s was bitten by a monkey. It was the first time a monkey bite had been recorded in the town.

Why have the monkeys become a problem? Some experts think the monkeys have moved into empty houses at the edge of the town. Like many places in Japan, Yugawara has a lot of empty houses because its population is getting smaller. A survey in 2024 found 433 empty houses in the town.

The town is trying different ways to deal with the problem. Officials have put GPS trackers on two of the troop's leaders to follow where the monkeys go. Teams also use firecrackers to scare the monkeys away before they cause trouble. The local government has asked people not to feed or annoy the monkeys.
If the problems continue, the town may have to catch some of the monkeys and put them to death to break up the troop.
The problem is worrying for local businesses. Yugawara depends on tourists who visit its hot springs and inns, and many people fear that visitors will stay away.
